title: Trump Is Expanding a Pledge That Could Stop AI Data Centers From Hiking Your Electricity Bill— Here's Who Just Signed On

The White House is expanding its voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge for AI data centers, adding nearly 200 utilities, governors, electricity cooperatives, public power providers and developers to the initiative, according to a White House official who confirmed the move to The Hill on Wednesday after The Wall Street Journal first reported the expansion.

The expanded pledge is intended to ensure companies building and powering AI data centers cover the costs of the electricity generation and transmission infrastructure needed for their projects instead of passing those expenses on to residential customers. Under the initiative, participating companies also agree to negotiate their own electricity rate structures with utilities and state governments.

The White House said Alphabet Inc., Microsoft Corp., Meta Platforms Inc., Oracle Corp, OpenAI, xAI and Amazon.com Inc. had already signed the pledge.

The White House said the additional signatories include major utilities such as
NextEra Energy, Inc. and Duke Energy Corp , along with electricity cooperatives, public power providers, data center developers and state governors. The administration said the expanded pledge now covers about 80% of the electricity delivered to U.S. homes and businesses.

"President Trump is expanding the Ratepayer Protection Pledge to governors, legislators, developers, and power providers to ensure everyone involved in building and powering data centers covers their own costs instead of passing them on to American families," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said in a statement.

Rogers said the initiative would help turn data centers into "engines of growth for local communities" while reinforcing U.S. leadership in the global AI race.

President Donald Trump is expected to formally announce the expanded initiative Thursday alongside Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin and Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry (R), Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp (R), Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen (R) and Idaho Gov. Brad Little (R)

Growing Demand

The expansion comes as AI infrastructure places increasing pressure on the U.S. power grid. Goldman Sachs estimates global data center electricity demand will climb 220% from 2023 levels by 2030, with about 60% of the additional demand expected to come from the United States. Data centers currently account for roughly 6% of U.S. electricity demand, a figure projected to rise to about 11% by the end of the decade.

一位白宫官员周三证实，在《华尔街日报》首次报道这一扩张计划后，白宫正在扩大其针对人工智能数据中心的自愿纳税人保护承诺，将近 200 家公用事业公司、州长、电力合作社、公共电力提供商和开发商纳入该计划。

扩大的承诺旨在确保人工智能数据中心的建设和供电公司承担其项目所需的发电和输电基础设施的成本，而不是将这些费用转嫁给住宅客户。 根据该倡议，参与公司还同意与公用事业公司和州政府协商自己的电价结构。

白宫表示，Alphabet Inc.、微软公司、Meta Platforms Inc.、甲骨文公司、OpenAI、xAI 和亚马逊公司已经签署了该承诺。

白宫表示，其他签署方包括 NextEra Energy, Inc. 和 Duke Energy Corp. 等主要公用事业公司，以及电力合作社、公共电力提供商、数据中心开发商和州长。 政府表示，扩大的承诺目前覆盖了向美国家庭和企业输送的约 80% 的电力。

白宫发言人泰勒·罗杰斯在一份声明中表示：“特朗普总统正在将纳税人保护承诺扩大到州长、立法者、开发商和电力供应商，以确保参与数据中心建设和供电的每个人都能承担自己的费用，而不是将其转嫁给美国家庭。”

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

罗杰斯表示，该举措将有助于将数据中心转变为“当地社区的增长引擎”，同时加强美国在全球人工智能竞赛中的领导地位。

预计唐纳德·特朗普总统将于周四与能源部长克里斯·赖特、环境保护局局长李·泽尔丁和路易斯安那州州长一起正式宣布扩大计划。 杰夫·兰德里（右），佐治亚州州长 布莱恩·坎普（右），内布拉斯加州州长 吉姆·皮伦（右）和爱达荷州州长。 布拉德·利特尔（右）

需求不断增长

这一扩张正值人工智能基础设施给美国电网带来越来越大的压力之际。 高盛预计，到 2030 年，全球数据中心电力需求将比 2023 年的水平增长 220%，其中约 60% 的新增需求预计将来自美国。 数据中心目前约占美国电力需求的 6%，预计到本世纪末这一数字将升至 11% 左右。
